purpose: Test whether the already legal current-season state decomposition and explicit context products transfer when learned by a strongly regularized low-capacity HGB instead of the previously tested CatBoost family.

novelty_audit.existing_current_state_runs: current_state_full/context/level were tested with CatBoost and CatBoost-outcome only
novelty_audit.existing_hgb_runs: HGB runs used base/e14 or prior-decay/player encodings, not the full D plus X/H1 current-state bundle
novelty_audit.external_research_boundary: A public implementation motivated the model-family hypothesis only. No external data, predictions, model artifacts, or copied source code enter this experiment.

data_rules.fit_game_type: R only because the official evaluation route is R
data_rules.history_rule: season strictly before target year for labels, state priors, and TrackMan profiles

structural_ablation.candidate_only_change: Add the deterministic 13 raw current-season state values, eight success/middle context products, and six ball/reverse/strike level products.

development_gate.primary_metric: paired normalized R Brier gain of candidate over exact HGB parent
development_gate.uncertainty: pitcher-cluster bootstrap 95% interval with 1000 fixed-seed replicates
requirements: positive R point gain over exact parent in both 2022 and 2023
positive R 95% gain lower bound over exact parent in both 2022 and 2023
positive R point gain over both honest R anchors in both 2022 and 2023
development_gate.on_fail: reject this HGB state/context recipe without running 2024
development_gate.on_pass: freeze this exact recipe, then run 2024 once and test convex blending against exact C and both honest anchors
